responsibility: Defines the common Darwin target configuration macros used when building GCC for Mach-O systems. It sets fundamental ABI types and object-format properties, driver self-specs and deployment-version defaults, linker/toolchain feature thresholds, pragma registration, include and framework hooks, exception-data encoding rules, section/anchor policies, builtin and C++ ABI hooks, and numerous assembler/linker conventions specific to Darwin. Unlike darwin.cc, this header expresses the target contract mostly through macros, specs, and hook definitions rather than implementing the logic.
same_name_distinction: This is the declarative target-configuration header in the Darwin group: it defines Darwin macros, specs, hook bindings, ABI/object-format settings, and driver policy, while darwin.cc implements the underlying target logic and darwin.opt only lists command-line option metadata.
